title: ISO 37301 vs the DOJ Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs: how do they compare on training?
description: ISO 37301 is a certifiable compliance management system standard; the DOJ ECCP is prosecutor guidance on program effectiveness. How they treat training.
shortAnswer: ISO 37301:2021 is an international standard that sets certifiable requirements for a compliance management system, including competence, training from the start of employment and at planned intervals, and awareness. The US Department of Justice (DOJ) Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs (ECCP), last updated in September 2024, is guidance prosecutors use to judge whether a company's program was effective when misconduct occurred. ISO 37301 tells an organization what to build; the ECCP shows how prosecutors will test whether it works.
keyTakeaways: ISO 37301 is voluntary and certifiable; the ECCP is not a standard and offers no certification, but its assessment can affect the form of resolution, penalties and monitorships.
ISO 37301 clause 7.2.3 requires training for relevant personnel from the start of employment and at planned intervals; clause 7.3 covers awareness, including how to raise concerns.
The ECCP asks who was trained and why, whether training covers prior incidents, how effectiveness is measured, and whether it changed behavior.
The ECCP does not reference ISO 37301, and ISO/TC 309 says use of the standard does not offer absolute protection against prosecution.
A program built to ISO 37301 and evidenced to the ECCP's effectiveness questions covers both the design and the results.

sections.heading: What is the core difference between ISO 37301 and the DOJ ECCP?

blocks.text: The core difference is purpose and audience. ISO 37301 is a requirements standard for organizations building a compliance management system, which a certification body can audit. The ECCP is an internal guide for federal prosecutors, published so companies can see the questions they will be asked after misconduct comes to light.

According to the [ISO/TC 309 FAQ](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc309/files/FAQ%2037301/ISO%2037301%20FAQs,%20May%202022.pdf), ISO 37301 was published on April 13, 2021, is voluntary but may become a legal or contractual requirement, is capable of certification, and its use may serve as evidence of adequate measures without offering absolute protection against prosecution. It replaced the guidance standard ISO 19600:2014. Detail is on [ISO 37301 compliance training requirements](/regulations/iso-37301-compliance-training-requirements).

The [ECCP](https://www.justice.gov/media/1160391/dl?inline) is meant to help prosecutors decide the form of any resolution or prosecution, any monetary penalty, and compliance obligations such as a monitorship. It frames three fundamental questions from the Justice Manual: "Is the corporation's compliance program well designed?", "Is the program being applied earnestly and in good faith?" and "Does the corporation's compliance program work in practice?" Its topics "form neither a checklist nor a formula." Detail is on [DOJ compliance program training expectations](/regulations/doj-compliance-program-training-expectations).

sections.heading: What does each expect of compliance training?

blocks.text: ISO 37301 requires a defined training process tied to competence and employment; the ECCP looks for evidence that training was targeted at risk and actually worked. The two are complementary: one sets the structure, the other sets the test.

ISO 37301 clause 7.2 covers competence for people whose work affects compliance performance, 7.2.2 brings compliance into the employment process, including due diligence and disciplinary action for noncompliance, and 7.2.3 covers training. Clause 7.3 awareness includes the compliance policy, how it affects people and which obligations apply to them, how to raise concerns, and the importance of supporting a compliance culture. Clause text is paywalled; this summary follows ISO's published contents and reputable certification body descriptions.

blocks.title: DOJ ECCP, section I.C, Training and Communications
blocks.text: "Prosecutors should also assess whether the training adequately covers prior compliance incidents and how the company measures the effectiveness of its training curriculum."

The ECCP's sample questions ask what analysis the company has done to decide who should be trained and on what, whether high risk and control employees get tailored training, whether supervisors get supplementary training, whether employees can ask questions, how the company addresses employees who fail testing, and whether training has changed employee behavior or operations.

blocks.text: Any organization that could face US federal criminal exposure should expect to be judged against the ECCP, whatever standard it follows. ISO 37301 is a choice: useful for organizations that want an auditable, international structure or certification to show customers and partners.

items: **US exposure:** design and evidence training to the ECCP questions, because they describe how effectiveness will be judged. The ECCP sits alongside other DOJ policies, including the Corporate Enforcement and Voluntary Self-Disclosure Policy.

**International footprint:** use ISO 37301 as the management system backbone, since it is not tied to one jurisdiction, and map local regimes such as [Portugal's anti-corruption regime](/regulations/portugal-anti-corruption-regime-training) or the [failure to prevent foreign bribery offense](/regulations/failure-to-prevent-foreign-bribery-training) onto it.

**Both:** many organizations build to ISO 37301 and keep an evidence pack organized around the ECCP's three questions. Certification does not settle the ECCP assessment, but the records it requires are a strong starting point.
**Measuring effectiveness:** see [how to evidence training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps compliance obligations, roles and risks to learning outcomes and assessment points, with provenance to ISO 37301 clauses and to the ECCP's questions. Prior incidents can be linked to the outcomes they should change, so the program can show both its design and its effect.

faqs.q: Does ISO 37301 certification protect a company from DOJ prosecution?
faqs.a: No. ISO/TC 309 states that using the standard may serve as evidence of adequate measures but does not offer absolute protection against prosecution, and the ECCP does not reference ISO 37301. Prosecutors make an individualized determination based on how the program was designed, resourced and worked in practice.

faqs.q: Is the ECCP only relevant to US companies?
faqs.a: It is written for federal prosecutors evaluating companies in DOJ Criminal Division matters, so its direct relevance depends on exposure to US federal criminal enforcement. Outside that context, many organizations use its questions as a practical benchmark for effectiveness because they are specific, public and focused on evidence that a program works.

faqs.q: How often does ISO 37301 require compliance training?
faqs.a: It does not fix a number. Clause 7.2.3 requires training from the start of employment and at planned intervals determined by the organization, so the organization sets the frequency based on risk and must be able to justify it. The ECCP also asks about periodic training and certification.

faqs.q: Is there guidance on competence under ISO 37301?
faqs.a: Yes. ISO 37303:2025, Compliance management systems: Guidance for competence management, gives guidance on determining and developing the competencies needed to achieve compliance management system objectives, including for internal functions and third parties.
